title: About Me
text:
I am a statistician, data analyst, and data scientist with a background in biology, and I specialize in turning complex data into evidence that informs decisions. My research training in ecology, microbiology, genomics, epidemiology, nutrition, and public health gave me a foundation in cross-sectional and longitudinal data across very different domains. I currently serve as a Lead Biostatistician and NIH R01 Co-Investigator at the Saban Research Institute within Children’s Hospital Los Angeles, leading statistical analyses, data visualization, and data science for a multi-institution research center.


My work spans four institutions (Children’s Hospital Los Angeles, the Keck School of Medicine at USC, UC San Diego, and Kaiser Permanente) and dozens of projects. As a statistician, I design studies and build statistical models. As a data analyst and engineer, I integrate dozens of datasets, including anthropometric, dietary, continuous glucose monitor, accelerometer, and at-home blood-sampling data, into analysis-ready form. As a data scientist, I apply machine learning to uncover patterns that traditional methods miss. My current focus is pediatric endocrinology, diabetes, and metabolism, but the same methods apply to any sensor, wearable, or longitudinal data, in health or beyond.


Communicating clearly is central to how I work. I have a strong reputation for explaining complex findings in writing and in person to audiences ranging from clinicians and investigators to administrators and trainees. I begin every project by defining the core question and the decision it needs to support, then evaluate it from several analytical perspectives, such as a mixed-effects model alongside gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost) on longitudinal clinical data, and compare the results before drawing conclusions.


I work in regulated research environments, where I document my code, build reproducible workflows, and submit my work for formal review. I also mentor students, postdocs, and clinicians in applying data to their work.


Tools: R, Python, SQL, SAS · Shiny, Quarto, GitHub


Outside of work, I enjoy running and hiking with my dog, photography, traveling, lifting weights, and following sports. Explore my projects or get in touch.

SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH EXPERIENCE & THEMES







Endocrinology, Diabetes, and Metabolism
Children’s Hospital Los Angeles
In my current role at CHLA, I serve as the lead biostatistician on multiple longitudinal clinical studies investigating how diet influences glycemic control in adolescents, children, and infants. I integrate continuous glucose monitoring data, dietary data, and statistical modeling to evaluate metabolic outcomes. In parallel, I work as a data engineer, managing data frames for several multi-institutional clinical studies through programming and data infrastructure maintenance.
2024 - Present


Microbial Genomics & Ecology
University of California, Santa Barbara
During my Ph.D., I investigated how marine biofilms develop under varying environmental conditions across ocean depths. I assessed depth-specific community formation by analyzing changes in bacterial diversity over time using 16S rRNA sequencing, amplicon sequence variants, statistical modeling, and bioinformatics. I also generated metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) to characterize the metabolic capacity of individual bacteria, with a focus on carbohydrate catabolism through CAZyme analysis.
2018 - 2024


Natural Product Discovery
Zymergen Inc. (acquired by Ginkgo Bioworks)
As part of a bioinformatics research group, I analyzed long-read soil microbiome sequences to identify biosynthetic gene clusters with potential to produce novel, patentable secondary metabolites. I used computational approaches including metagenomic assembly, predictive metabolic software, and custom coding to characterize these clusters. This work supported downstream investigation and validation of high-value metabolites.
2021


Quantitative Ecology
California State University, Los Angeles
I used fieldwork, remote sensing, and statistical modeling to assess how the Los Angeles urban forest supports wildlife across socioeconomic gradients in the Los Angeles basin. I used birds as model organisms to evaluate how native and non-native street trees provide ecosystem resources to urban wildlife. Specifically, I identified which non-native trees offer resources comparable to native species and analyzed how socioeconomic factors influence urban bird diversity.
2016 - 2018


Developmental & Molecular Biology
California Institute of Technology (CalTech)
I used plasmid cloning, bacterial transformation, immunohistochemistry, embryology, and live-cell confocal imaging targeting green fluorescent protein to investigate neural crest cell migration during chicken embryonic development. My work focused on visualizing cellular movement in vivo. Specifically, I examined how neural crest cells migrate toward developing sensory organs.
2015


Cell & Molecular Biology
California State University, Los Angeles
I used molecular techniques including restriction enzyme digestion, plasmid cloning, bacterial transformations, transient transfections, and luciferase reporter assays to investigate actin expression in developing skeletal muscle cells. My work focused on quantifying transcriptional regulation in myoblasts. Specifically, I evaluated how MyoD influences actin expression during muscle development.
2013 - 2015
